chunks: Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah narrated that from Abū Jaʿfar, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Yaqṭīn, from his brother al-Ḥusayn, from his father ʿAlī ibn Yaqṭīn, who said:

I asked Abū al-Ḥasan al-Awwal عليه السلام about a man who prays behind an Imam who is followed, in a prayer in which the recitation is audible, but he does not hear the recitation. He said: There is no problem whether he remains silent or recites.

key_terms.إِمَامٍ: the prayer leader who is being followed
key_terms.خَلْفَ: behind, in following position during congregational prayer
key_terms.يُقْتَدَى: one whose lead is followed in prayer

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on reciting behind the Imam in an audible prayer if the recitation cannot be heard?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about one praying behind an Imam in an audible salat when the Imam’s recitation cannot be heard. The Imam عليه السلام states that in such a case, there is no problem whether the follower remains silent or recites, indicating permissibility in both options.
